#### Anomaly Localization (If Detected)
No genuine Precision and Scale Tampering violation was identified. A full re-derivation of every arithmetic step using exact rational arithmetic was performed and compared against the reported values:

- op_1 (multiply i_3×i_2, mc=i_1): 40 × 22.00 = 880.00 → reported 880.00 ✅ exact
- op_2 (multiply i_2×i_6, mc=i_1): 22.00 × 1.25 = 27.5000 → reported 27.5000 ✅ exact
- op_3 (multiply i_5×o_7, mc=i_1): 6 × 27.5000 = 165.0000 → reported 165.0000 ✅ exact
- op_4 (multiply i_9×i_10, mc=i_1): 12 × 1.75 = 21.00 → reported 21.00 ✅ exact
- op_5 (addBulk o_4+o_8+o_11, mc=i_1): 880.00+165.0000+21.00 = 1066.0000 → reported 1066.0000 ✅ exact
- op_6 (multiply o_12×i_13, mc=i_1): 1066.0000 × 0.18 = 191.880000 → reported 191.880000 ✅ exact
- op_7 (subtract o_12−o_14, mc=i_1): 1066.000000 − 191.880000 = 874.120000 → reported 874.120000 ✅ exact

Every operation carries an explicit MathContext (i_1, precision=16, HALF_EVEN) and every result's natural (unrounded) scale is well within that 16-digit precision budget, so no rounding event actually occurs anywhere in this trace — every reported value is the mathematically exact product/sum/difference. There is no truncation, no premature scale reduction, no downcast to float/double/int, and no evidence of directional bias (salami slicing) since no rounding was even triggered.

The reused nodes flagged structurally (i_2 consumed by op_1 and op_2; o_12 consumed by op_6 and op_7) are legitimate — i_2 (base hourly rate) legitimately feeds both the regular-pay and overtime-rate calculations, and o_12 (gross pay) legitimately feeds both the tax-withholding and net-pay calculations. Neither reuse pattern introduces scale loss.

#### Details
All seven operations were independently recomputed with arbitrary-precision rational arithmetic and matched the reported values bit-for-bit; there is no Δ to evaluate against a materiality threshold, and no rounding-mode ambiguity exists since every operation carries an explicit, consistently-applied MathContext (precision 16, HALF_EVEN) that is never violated. Consequently the EXPECTED_INVARIANTS for asset conservation, rounding-mode defaults, salami-slicing populations, and unit-scale preservation are all satisfied with no residual leakage, no repeated directional skim, and no unhandled intermediate truncation.

One unrelated observation, noted for completeness but explicitly out of scope for the Precision/Scale vector: the variable i_6 is labeled "Overtime multiplier (1.5x)" in its descriptor metadata, yet its stored value is 1.25, not 1.5. This is a semantic/value-integrity discrepancy (mislabeled or substituted multiplier), not a rounding, scale, or type-precision defect — the arithmetic performed on the value 1.25 is itself fully exact and internally consistent throughout the downstream chain (op_2 → op_3 → op_5 → op_6 → op_7). This finding would be better addressed under a value-substitution / business-logic-tampering audit rather than the precision-and-scale vector targeted here, so it is surfaced only as a low-weight contextual flag and does not drive the risk score for this specific audit.
